text.p: Following are some of the main stories in Dutch newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
HET FINANCIEELE DAGBLAD
- Dutch central bank warns financial services group Fortis' Belgian unit NMKN for addvertising to Dutch investors. (p1)
- Department store group KBB shares plummet eight percent after profit warning. (p1)
- Labour party demands loyalty from its coalition partners D66 and Liberal VVD over minimum wage. (p1)
- Some 100 workers at Belgium steel company Boel block referendum on restructuring plan. (p3)
- Amsterdam cable operator A2000 and PTT Telecom sign agreement on interconnecting phone calls. (p3)
- Royal Dutch/Shell is to ban pornographic magazines and vidoes from its petrol station shops. (p3)
- Dutch consumer confidence jumps to +12 in January, according to Dutch statistics office CBS. (p5)
DE VOLKSKRANT
- Rotterdam, Amsterdam and The Hague support the city of Apeldoorn in its refusal to put asylum seekers on the street after application for asylum fails. (p1)
- Transhipment firm EBS on the verge of bankruptcy after employees' rejection of accord between unions and firm. (p2)
- Deadlock in takeover attempt of newspaper Het Financieele Dagblad by British publisher Pearson. (p2)
- Former Philips Electronics president Jan Timmer sees no sign of criticism from his successor Cor Boonstra. (p2)
DE TELEGRAAF
- Number of car thefts drops by 8.5 pct last year after years of rising steadily. (p1)
- Reorganisation at ABN AMRO headoffice brings savings of 100 million guilders. (p1)
- Restructuring of railway builder Strukton is to cost 40 of the 2,000 jobs. (p23)
TROUW
- Ministry of transport and public works is planning a new airport in the sea to handle 80 million passengers a year. (p1)
- Realty fund Sarakreek buys Eastern Realty Investment for $185 million. (p7)
ALGEMEEN DAGBLAD
- Russian president Boris Yeltsin has to cancel his visit to the Netherlands because of his health. (p1)
